name: $schema
text: The address of the latest version of this schema, the same as its $id. Written as the first key of the document; any string is read.

name: schemaVersion
shape: str const: the UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of this schema last changed.
text: The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the shape of this schema last changed.

name: buildVersion
shape: UtcInstant, required, 3rd property (right after $schema and schemaVersion)
text: The UTC time (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ) when the GRS build that wrote this file was made. It is for finding bugs: it tells which build wrote the file. To know whether you can read a document, check only schemaVersion.

name: schedule
text: The data: what is exported to MS Project, and what GRS adds to draw it.

name: schedule.project
text: The one project of this document: its own particulars and its calendar defaults.

name: schedule.calendars
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The calendars of the document; working days are counted with the one calendar that project.calendarUid names.

name: schedule.tasks
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The tasks. Their WBS tree is given by Task.parentTaskUid and Task.siblingOrder.

name: schedule.resources
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The people, or other resources, that work can be assigned to.

name: schedule.assignments
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Which resource works on which task.

name: schedule.taskGroups
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The task groups: the rows of the task group panel, each task group one row (a band on the chart). A task group can sit under a parent task group (TaskGroup.parentId), and taskGroupMembers says which tasks are drawn in it.

name: schedule.taskGroupMembers
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Which task group each task is drawn in: one entry per task, from taskUid to taskGroupId. A task group in taskGroups can hold many tasks, but each task sits in exactly one task group.

name: schedule.taskVisuals
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: How each task is drawn (shape, colors and outline width): exactly one entry per task.

name: schedule.taskOrigins
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: One record per task that came from an imported MS Project file: which file and which task in it, so that a later import of the same file updates that task instead of adding a copy. A task made in GRS has no record.

name: schedule.baselineTasks
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The plan as it was before: a saved copy of earlier task dates, matched to the current tasks by uid and drawn as an outline over them for comparison.

name: schedule.commentBoxes
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Notes placed on the chart; each one points at a task, a highlight box or a free point.

name: schedule.highlightBoxes
shape: array, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Rectangles on the chart that mark a range of days over a range of task groups, drawn with a frame, a fill or both.

name: documentSettings
text: How the document is drawn when it is opened. Keys that always have a value are always written, so that a later change of a product default does not change the picture.

name: documentSettings.displayScalePercent
text: Display scale of the schedule drawing, in percent. At 100, every ...Px value is drawn as that many CSS pixels; at 50, it is drawn at half size. It scales the shapes and the text of the schedule together. It does not change the app header or the command palette, and it is not the browser's own zoom. The document opens at this value; a reader who changes it edits the document.

name: documentSettings.fontSizeStep
text: Text size step of the schedule: the reader's choice of text size. small is 7.5, medium 8.75 and large 10 CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100, before the tool's own ratios. The document opens at this step; a reader who changes it edits the document.

name: documentSettings.dayWidthPx
text: Width of one calendar day on the time axis, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. Fit to screen sets it so that the whole schedule fits the width of the screen.

name: documentSettings.verticalZoomRatio
text: Vertical size of the task figures, as a ratio to the default size. 1 is the default size; 2 draws plan bars, actual bars and task name labels twice as tall. It is never below 1. How deep task groups open is set by taskGroupAutoExpandDepth.

name: documentSettings.taskGroupAutoExpandDepth
text: How deep task groups with treeState auto open. A top-level task group is depth 1. Task groups open down to this depth, so their children are shown down to depth taskGroupAutoExpandDepth + 1. 0 draws only the top-level task groups, closed. A task group that a person opened or closed keeps its own treeState.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition
text: Where the view starts when the document opens: notDecided lets GRS choose, placed gives the day at the left edge and the task group at the top edge.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition/oneOf[*].kind
text: notDecided: no person has chosen a place yet, and GRS chooses one when it opens the document; placed: the other keys give the place.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition/oneOf[placed].leftEdgeDay
text: The day at the left edge of the view.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition/oneOf[placed].leftEdgeDayFraction
text: Where the left edge falls inside leftEdgeDay, as a part of that day; 0 is the start of the day.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition/oneOf[placed].topEdgeTaskGroupId
text: The task group at the top edge of the view. When that task group is deleted, scrollPosition becomes notDecided.

name: documentSettings.scrollPosition/oneOf[placed].topEdgeTaskGroupFraction
text: Where the top edge falls inside that task group, as a part of its step (its band height plus the gap below it), not in pixels; 0 is its top.

name: documentSettings.fitSpan
shape: object {firstDay,lastDay,isFixed}, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no fit span
text: The fit span: firstDay..lastDay (both days included) and isFixed. When isFixed is true, Fit and picture export show this span instead of the whole schedule. Opening the document does not move the view. Absent means no fit span.

name: documentSettings.fitSpan.firstDay
text: The first day of the fit span (included), as a day of the shown clock (viewTimeZone).

name: documentSettings.fitSpan.lastDay
text: The last day of the fit span; its column is included.

name: documentSettings.fitSpan.isFixed
text: When true, Fit and picture export show the fit span instead of the whole schedule; opening the document does not move the view.

name: documentSettings.viewTimeZone
text: The time zone that the time ruler and the shown date-times use: sameAsScheduleData follows project.scheduleDataTimeZone, fixed uses the offset given here.

name: documentSettings.viewTimeZone/oneOf[*].kind
text: sameAsScheduleData: show the schedule data time zone, and follow it when it changes; fixed: show the offset given here.

name: documentSettings.viewTimeZone/oneOf[fixed].offset
text: The UTC offset that the chart is shown in.

name: documentSettings.displayTimeZones
shape: {offset:UtcOffset, season:standard|daylight}[] 1..4, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Up to four extra clocks, each shown as one more row under the time ruler while the time of day is shown.

name: documentSettings.displayTimeZones[].offset
text: The UTC offset of this extra clock.

name: documentSettings.displayTimeZones[].season
text: Whether this clock is the standard-time or the daylight-time zone of its offset. It picks the zone name that is shown; the offset itself is used all year.

name: documentSettings.isTimeOfDayVisible
text: Whether the time of day is shown on the chart; the stored date-times keep their time either way. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isPlanVisible
text: Whether plan bars are shown, apart from isActualVisible. A new document starts with true.

name: documentSettings.isPlanDatesVisible
text: Whether the planned dates are shown to the right of each task name label. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isActualVisible
text: Whether actual bars are shown, apart from isPlanVisible. A new document starts with true.

name: documentSettings.isPercentCompleteVisible
text: Whether the percent complete label of each task is shown. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isBaselineVisible
text: Whether the earlier plan (baselineTasks) is drawn over the current tasks. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isProgressLineVisible
text: Whether the progress line is drawn: the line from the status date through the progress point of each task. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isProgressMarkerVisible
text: Whether progress markers and resume icons are drawn; while Delay Diagnostics is shown, markers are drawn even when this is false. A new document starts with true.

name: documentSettings.isDependencyVisible
text: Whether dependency lines are drawn. A new document starts with true.

name: documentSettings.isAssigneeVisible
text: Whether the assignee label of each task is shown. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isDateGridLinesVisible
text: Whether vertical date grid lines are drawn. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.isGroupGridLinesVisible
text: Whether lines between task groups are drawn, on the chart and in the task group panel. A new document starts with true.

name: documentSettings.stackDirection
text: up stacks a task group's tasks so that the chart climbs to a goal at the upper right; down stacks them so that it descends to a goal at the lower right. A new document starts with up.

name: documentSettings.isThemeMonochrome
text: Whether the theme is monochrome. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.taskGroupPanelWidthPx
text: Width of the task group panel, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100.

name: documentSettings.isTaskGroupPanelWidthFixed
text: Whether the task group panel width is set by the number taskGroupPanelWidthPx instead of by dragging the panel border. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.levelZeroTreeState
text: The tree state of level 0, the head of the task group panel: collapsed draws no task group at all. A new document starts with auto.

name: documentSettings.pinnedTaskGroupIds
shape: uuid[] 1..5, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The task groups pinned in a band at the top of the chart, to compare them with task groups far away. Absent means none is pinned.

name: documentSettings.tableViews
text: How the three tables are shown: the Search Panel, the Delay Diagnostics Report and the Resource List.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.searchPanel
text: How the tables of the Search Panel are shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.searchPanel.isScheduleFilterApplied
text: Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.searchPanel.shownTaskUids
shape: int 0..2147483647[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The tasks whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.searchPanel.columnFilters
shape: ColumnFilter[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The column filters of the Search Panel tables (the task table and the comment box table), one per filtered column, by the column names of those tables. Absent means no column is filtered.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.searchPanel.sort
shape: ColumnSort, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.delayDiagnosticsReport
text: How the Delay Diagnostics Report table is shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.delayDiagnosticsReport.isScheduleFilterApplied
text: Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.delayDiagnosticsReport.shownTaskUids
shape: int 0..2147483647[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The tasks whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.delayDiagnosticsReport.columnFilters
shape: ColumnFilter[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The column filters of the Delay Diagnostics Report table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column is filtered.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.delayDiagnosticsReport.sort
shape: ColumnSort, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList
text: How the Resource List table is shown: schedule filter, checked rows, column filters and sort.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList.isScheduleFilterApplied
text: Whether the schedule filter of this table is on; while it is on, the chart draws only what the checked rows of this table select. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList.shownResourceUids
shape: int 0..2147483647[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The resources whose row is checked in the show column of this table. Absent means no row is checked.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList.isUnassignedShown
text: Whether the (no assignee) row of the Resource List is checked. A new document starts with false.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList.columnFilters
shape: ColumnFilter[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The column filters of the Resource List table, one per filtered column, by the column names of that table. Absent means no column is filtered.

name: documentSettings.tableViews.resourceList.sort
shape: ColumnSort, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: default order
text: How this table is sorted. Absent means the default order.

name: documentStamp
text: The stamp of the document: when it last changed and was saved, and who wrote it last.

name: changeLogEntries
shape: ChangeLogEntry[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The reasons for changes, one entry per recorded change.

name: Project
text: The project's own particulars, and the calendar defaults that apply to the whole document.

name: Project.id
text: MS Project's Project/UID. Not a key: a document holds one project. Absent when the file had none.

name: Project.calendarUid
text: MS Project's CalendarUID: the calendar of the document; working days are counted with this one calendar.

name: Project.name
text: The project name of the MS Project exchange format (Project/Name). GRS reads it from that format and writes it back. GRS does not show it; the name shown on screen is title. Absent when the file had none.

name: Project.title
text: The document title: the name shown on screen at the top of the page, and the default name of an exported file. Read it to tell which document is open. Absent means untitled; the screen shows Untitled.

name: Project.subject
text: MS Project's Subject: the subject of the project.

name: Project.category
text: MS Project's Category: the category of the project.

name: Project.company
text: MS Project's Company: the company name.

name: Project.manager
text: MS Project's Manager: the name of the manager.

name: Project.author
text: MS Project's Author: who made the project, not who wrote it last.

name: Project.revision
text: MS Project's Revision: how many times MS Project saved the file; it is not one of the documentStamp times.

name: Project.creationDate
text: MS Project's CreationDate: a local date-time, like the schedule dates. GRS writes it when it makes a new document, and keeps an imported one. Absent when the file had none.

name: Project.startDate
text: MS Project's StartDate: the start of the project, a date-time that is drawn on its day.

name: Project.statusDate
text: MS Project's StatusDate: progress is reported on this day. The status line and the progress line are drawn on its day, so its time of day does not move them. Absent means no status date: no status line is drawn and Delay Diagnostics does not run.

name: Project.scheduleDataTimeZone
text: The fixed UTC offset whose wall clock the schedule date-times are, as a standard-time key such as UTC+09:00. Daylight saving is never applied by season. Not written to MS Project, which has no place for it.

name: Project.minutesPerDay
text: The length of 1d in durations and lags, in minutes (480 when absent). Keep it equal to the working minutes of every working day, including one-off working exception days (a day with no spans of its own counts the default spans). When a day differs, GRS reports it each time the document opens, because 1d would then no longer be one working day.

name: Project.minutesPerWeek
text: MS Project's MinutesPerWeek: the length of one week, in minutes.

name: Project.daysPerMonth
text: MS Project's DaysPerMonth: the length of one month, in days.

name: Project.weekStartDay
text: MS Project's numbering: 0 Sunday ... 6 Saturday (one less than WeekDay.dayType). Absent means Monday (1), the default of settings row S-108.

name: Project.defaultStartTime
text: MS Project's DefaultStartTime: the time GRS writes on start-side dates; 08:00:00 when absent.

name: Project.defaultFinishTime
text: MS Project's DefaultFinishTime: the time GRS writes on finish-side dates; 17:00:00 when absent.

name: Project.themeHueDegrees
text: The hue of the theme, used by every color written as {"kind":"theme"}; it belongs to the project, not to the reader, so it is here and not in documentSettings. A new document starts with 214.

name: Project.parentTaskProgressToleranceWorkingDays
text: How many working days a parent task's progress point may lie outside the progress points of the work below it before Delay Diagnostics asks whether an update is missing. It belongs to the project, not to the reader; a new document starts with 1.

name: Project.highestIssuedUid
text: One counter for the uids of tasks, resources, assignments and calendars. Uids are never reused, so a new uid is always above this value, up to 2147483647.

name: Project.lastImportNumber
text: How many times a file has been imported into this document; 0 means never. TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportNumber is compared with it.

name: Project.firstOutlineLevel
text: The OutlineLevel at which the tasks of an imported file start (the project summary task is not counted); export writes from this number. A new document starts with 1.

name: Project.sourceFormat
text: The format the document came from: grs for a document made in GRS, pj12 or pj15 for an MS Project file (pj15 when it has any element that only pj15 has). It is not exported to MS Project.

name: Project.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Project.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: Calendar
text: One calendar. Decides which days are worked and which are not.

name: Calendar.uid
text: MS Project's UID: the id of the calendar.

name: Calendar.baseCalendarUid
text: MS Project's BaseCalendarUID: the calendar that this one inherits from.

name: Calendar.ordinal
text: The order of the calendar as it came in the file, used to write the calendars back in that order.

name: Calendar.name
text: MS Project's Name: the calendar name.

name: Calendar.isBaseCalendar
text: MS Project's IsBaseCalendar: whether this is a base calendar; absent reads as false.

name: Calendar.weekDays
shape: WeekDay[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project's WeekDays: whether each day of the week is worked.

name: Calendar.exceptions
shape: Exception[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project's Exceptions: the days that differ from the normal week.

name: Calendar.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Calendar.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: WeekDay
text: Whether one day of the week is worked.

name: WeekDay.ordinal
text: The order of this weekday within its calendar, as it came in the file.

name: WeekDay.dayType
text: MS Project's numbering: 1 Sunday ... 7 Saturday (one more than Project.weekStartDay).

name: WeekDay.dayWorking
text: MS Project's DayWorking: whether this day of the week is worked; absent reads as not working.

name: WeekDay.workingTimes
shape: WorkingTime[] 1..5, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Absent on a working day means the default spans 08:00-12:00, 13:00-17:00.

name: WeekDay.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: WeekDay.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: Exception
text: An exception to a calendar's week, possibly recurring.

name: Exception.ordinal
text: The order of this exception within its calendar, as it came in the file.

name: Exception.name
text: MS Project's Name: the name of the exception.

name: Exception.fromDate
text: For a one-off exception (see recurrenceKind), fromDate..toDate is the real range of days, written 00:00:00 and 23:59:00, and its workingTimes replace the spans of those days. For a recurring exception, it is MS Project's start of the recurrence, not a range of real days. Absent when the file had none.

name: Exception.toDate
text: MS Project's ToDate: the end of the range that fromDate starts (see fromDate).

name: Exception.dayWorking
text: MS Project's DayWorking: whether the exception days are worked; absent reads as not working.

name: Exception.recurrenceKind
text: MS Project's Exception/Type: 1 daily, 2 yearly by day of the month, 3 yearly by position, 4 monthly by day of the month, 5 monthly by position, 6 weekly, 7 by day count, 8 by weekday count, 9 none. A row is a one-off (non-recurring) exception when this is 9 or absent, or when it is 1 and recurrencePeriod is absent or 1. Any other row repeats and is not counted as days off. Write 1 for an exception you add.

name: Exception.recurrencePeriod
shape: int >=1, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: the file had no Period
text: MS Project's Exception/Period: the interval of the recurrence. Absent when the file had none.

name: Exception.workingTimes
shape: WorkingTime[] 1..5, optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: Absent on a working day means the default spans 08:00-12:00, 13:00-17:00.

name: Exception.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Exception.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: WorkingTime
text: One working span of a weekday or an exception day. The spans of one day start before they end and do not overlap; a span that ends at 12:00 and one that starts at 12:00 only touch, which is fine.

name: WorkingTime.ordinal
text: The order of this span within its day; GRS writes the spans in the order of their start.

name: WorkingTime.fromTime
text: MS Project's FromTime: the start of the working span.

name: WorkingTime.toTime
text: 00:00:00 here is the end of the day (24:00), as MS Project writes it. Absent when the file had none.

name: Task
text: One task: its plan, and its actual given by dates.

name: Task.uid
text: MS Project's UID: the id of the task, unique in the document and never changed; read no meaning into its value.

name: Task.parentTaskUid
shape: int 0..2147483647, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: top of the WBS
text: The parent task in the WBS. Absent means a top-level task.

name: Task.calendarUid
text: Kept only so that it goes back to MS Project unchanged. Working days are counted with the one calendar that project.calendarUid names. Absent when the file had none.

name: Task.siblingOrder
text: The order of this task among the tasks under the same parent task.

name: Task.name
text: MS Project's Task/Name. Absent means an unnamed task; the screen shows no name.

name: Task.notes
text: MS Project's Notes: the notes of the task.

name: Task.start
text: MS Project's Start: the planned start.

name: Task.finish
text: MS Project's Finish: the planned finish.

name: Task.milestone
text: The fact, exported to MS Project; absent means false. TaskVisual holds milestoneShape when it is true and taskShape otherwise.

name: Task.deadline
text: MS Project's Deadline: the deadline of the task.

name: Task.actualStart
text: MS Project's ActualStart: the actual start; absent means the task has not started.

name: Task.stop
text: MS Project's Stop. It keeps its MS Project name so that it goes back to MS Project unchanged. While the task is unfinished, it is the point in time that the actual work has reached. Absent once actualFinish is set.

name: Task.actualFinish
text: MS Project's ActualFinish: the actual finish; it is present only once the task is finished.

name: Task.resume
text: MS Project's Resume: the day the rest of an interrupted task is planned to restart. Absent means no restart is planned.

name: Task.resumeValid
text: MS Project's ResumeValid: false means interrupted with no restart day decided. Absent when the file had none.

name: Task.percentComplete
text: Follows from the dates: round(actual length / planned length x 100), both in working minutes of the document calendar. The actual runs from actualStart to actualFinish, or to stop while unfinished, so statusDate does not move it. With no planned length (a milestone), it is 100 once actualFinish is set and 0 before. GRS counts it again each time it reads this file and reports when the stored value was different, so write what the dates give. It has no upper limit of 100, because an overrun reports more. Absent when the file had none; GRS then counts it from the dates and writes it.

name: Task.fadeInCalendarDays
shape: int >=0, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no fade: default depth on chevrons; 0 = flat end
text: Calendar days at the start of the bar, inside start..finish. They are drawn slanted to show that the start is not yet firm. This is a fact about the task, so it is exported to MS Project and is not kept in TaskVisual. Absent means no fade (a chevron keeps its default notch); 0 is a flat end.

name: Task.fadeOutCalendarDays
shape: int >=0, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no fade: default depth on chevrons; 0 = flat end
text: As fadeInCalendarDays, for the finish.

name: Task.hyperlinkAddress
shape: str 1..512 (URL), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link
text: MS Project's HyperlinkAddress: the URL the task links to. Absent means no link.

name: Task.hyperlink
shape: str 1..512 (link title), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link title
text: MS Project's Hyperlink: the title of the link, not its address. Absent means no title.

name: Task.dependencies
shape: Dependency[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project's PredecessorLink: the dependencies in which this task is the successor.

name: Task.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Task.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: Dependency
text: One dependency, nested under the task that follows it, as MS Project nests it.

name: Dependency.predecessorUid
text: MS Project's PredecessorUID: the task that comes first; the successor is the task that this dependency is nested in.

name: Dependency.linkType
text: MS Project's codes: 0 finish-to-finish, 1 finish-to-start, 2 start-to-finish, 3 start-to-start.

name: Dependency.linkLag
text: MS Project's LinkLag, in tenths of a minute for every lagFormat. A working day (lagFormat 7) is project.minutesPerDay minutes, or 480 when that is absent. Absent means no lag.

name: Dependency.lagFormat
text: MS Project's LagFormat: the unit the lag is shown in. GRS reads 7 (working days), 5 (hours) and 3 (minutes), and writes the unit the lag was typed in. Any other value is kept but not counted. Absent when the file had none.

name: Dependency.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Dependency.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: Resource
text: One person to assign work to, or one resource.

name: Resource.uid
text: MS Project's UID: the id of the resource.

name: Resource.calendarUid
text: The same as Task.calendarUid. Absent when the file had none.

name: Resource.name
text: MS Project's Name: the resource name.

name: Resource.resourceKind
text: MS Project's Type: 0 material, 1 work, 2 cost. Absent when the file had none.

name: Resource.isCostResource
text: MS Project's IsCostResource: whether this is a cost resource; absent reads as false.

name: Resource.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Resource.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: Assignment
text: Which person is on which task.

name: Assignment.uid
text: MS Project's UID: the id of the assignment.

name: Assignment.taskUid
text: MS Project's TaskUID: the task that is worked on.

name: Assignment.resourceUid
text: MS Project's ResourceUID: the resource that works on the task.

name: Assignment.passthroughValues
shape: PassthroughValues (map str->str<=65535, >=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: nothing kept
text: MS Project values GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged. Absent when there are none.

name: Assignment.passthroughElements
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: MS Project child elements GRS does not interpret, kept in their places. Absent when there are none; never an empty list.

name: TaskGroup
text: A task group on screen. Task groups are kept apart from the WBS (Task.parentTaskUid) so that several tasks can share one task group; task groups are not exported to MS Project.

name: TaskGroup.id
text: The id of the task group.

name: TaskGroup.parentId
shape: uuid, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: top-level task group, depth 1
text: The parent task group. Absent means a top-level task group (depth 1).

name: TaskGroup.representedTaskUid
shape: int 0..2147483647, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: stands for no task in the WBS
text: The task this task group stands for in the WBS (Task.parentTaskUid). Absent means it stands for no task. It is not where the name comes from.

name: TaskGroup.siblingOrder
text: The order of this task group among the task groups under the same parent.

name: TaskGroup.name
shape: str 1..512, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no name; the screen shows an empty title
text: The task group name. Absent means an unnamed task group; the screen shows an empty title. GRS never copies a task name into it after the group exists.

name: TaskGroup.treeState
text: Whether the task group is open, closed or hidden in the task group panel. It is saved, like every task group state, so that reopening shows what was saved. A task group in auto opens down to documentSettings.taskGroupAutoExpandDepth.

name: TaskGroup.editGroup
shape: str 1..512, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: anyone may edit
text: The edit group this task group belongs to. Absent means anyone may edit it.

name: TaskGroup.color
shape: $ref BandColor, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no band colour drawn
text: The task group band color. Absent means no band color is drawn; {"kind":"theme"} draws the theme color.

name: TaskGroup.minHeightPx
shape: int >=1, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no lowest height
text: Lowest height of the task group's row, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100; absent means no lowest height. verticalZoomRatio does not change it.

name: TaskGroup.hyperlinkAddress
shape: str 1..512 (URL), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link
text: The URL the task group links to (MS Project's name). Absent means no link.

name: TaskGroup.hyperlink
shape: str 1..512 (link title), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link title
text: The title of the task group link. Absent means no title.

name: TaskGroupMember
text: Which task group a task sits on; every task sits on exactly one task group. No lane is stored: GRS stacks a task group's tasks itself, in the direction documentSettings.stackDirection names.

name: TaskGroupMember.taskUid
text: The task; each task is in exactly one entry.

name: TaskGroupMember.taskGroupId
text: The task group that the task is drawn in.

name: TaskVisual
text: How a task is drawn: its shape, its colors and its outline width. Every task has exactly one, so that no other way of drawing a task is needed.

name: TaskVisual.taskUid
text: The task that is drawn; each task has exactly one TaskVisual.

name: TaskVisual.taskShape
shape: enum rectangle|chevron|arrow|endpointSpan; required when Task.milestone is not true, absent on milestones
text: Shape of a task that is not a milestone: rectangle, chevron, arrow or endpointSpan. Present exactly when Task.milestone is not true; a milestone holds milestoneShape instead.

name: TaskVisual.milestoneShape
shape: enum 15 glyphs; required when Task.milestone is true, absent otherwise
text: Glyph of a milestone. Present exactly when Task.milestone is true.

name: TaskVisual.fillColor
shape: $ref Color, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: not drawn
text: Fill of the plan bar (and the base of the actual fill). Absent means no fill is drawn. A custom color may omit one side; GRS derives it on load (HSL lightness 1 - L) and marks it source "derived". Fill and stroke may not both be absent.

name: TaskVisual.strokeColor
shape: $ref Color, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: not drawn
text: Outline of the plan and actual bars. Absent means no outline is drawn. Same shape as fillColor.

name: TaskVisual.strokeWidthPx
text: Outline width of the task's plan and actual bars, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100 (1 to 10; GRS writes 1 for a new task).

name: TaskOrigin
text: Where an imported task came from, so that importing the same file again updates the task instead of adding a copy.

name: TaskOrigin.taskUid
text: The imported task in this document.

name: TaskOrigin.sourceProjectId
shape: str 1..16, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: the source file had no Project.id
text: Project/UID of the file this task was imported from. Absent when that file had none.

name: TaskOrigin.sourceUid
text: The UID of the task in the file that it was imported from.

name: TaskOrigin.importSessionId
text: The id of the import that brought the task in; every import makes a new one. It stands in for sourceProjectId when the file had no Project/UID.

name: TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportNumber
text: The project.lastImportNumber of the last import that found this task in its file.

name: BaselineTask
text: One task of an earlier plan, matched to the current task by uid and drawn only as an outline over it.

name: BaselineTask.uid
text: The uid of the task in the earlier plan; it is matched to the current task with the same uid.

name: BaselineTask.name
shape: str 1..512, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: the task had no name
text: The task name in the earlier plan.

name: BaselineTask.start
text: The planned start in the earlier plan.

name: BaselineTask.finish
text: The planned finish in the earlier plan.

name: BaselineTask.milestone
shape: bool, required (false when the source had none)
text: Whether the task was a milestone in the earlier plan, so that it is drawn as one.

name: CommentBox
text: One comment box. Its tip stands at a free point (an instant, a task group and a height within its band) or at one of eight points of the task or highlight box it snapped to.

name: CommentBox.id
text: The id of the comment box.

name: CommentBox.anchor
text: Where the leader line of the comment box points. It is a free point (a point in time, a task group and a height within its band), or one of eight points of the task or highlight box it snapped to. A snapped anchor also keeps a fallback task group and height, used when its target is deleted.

name: CommentBox.bodyOffsetPx
text: Offset from the anchor point to the lower-left corner of the comment box body, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100. It follows displayScalePercent, so the box keeps its place beside what it points at; zoom does not change it.

name: CommentBox.bodyOffsetPx.dx
text: The horizontal part of bodyOffsetPx. A positive value moves the box to the right.

name: CommentBox.bodyOffsetPx.dy
text: The vertical part of bodyOffsetPx. A positive value moves the box down, as on the screen.

name: CommentBox.text
shape: str 1..65535, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: empty body
text: The text of the comment box. Absent means an empty body.

name: CommentBox.fillColor
text: Fill color of the comment box body; fillTransparencyPercent 100 draws no fill.

name: CommentBox.fillTransparencyPercent
text: Transparency of the comment box fill in percent: 0 is opaque, 100 draws no fill.

name: CommentBox.strokeColor
text: Color of the comment box border and leader line.

name: CommentBox.strokeWidthPx
text: Width of the comment box's border and leader line, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100 (1 to 10; GRS writes 1 when it places a box). It follows displayScalePercent; zoom does not change it.

name: CommentBox.textColor
text: Color of the comment box text.

name: CommentBox.fontSizePx
text: Text size of the comment box, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100 (8 to 24; GRS writes 10 when it places a box). It follows displayScalePercent like the rest of the drawing; zoom does not change it.

name: CommentBox.hyperlinkAddress
shape: str 1..512 (URL), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link
text: The URL the comment box links to (MS Project's name). Absent means no link.

name: CommentBox.hyperlink
shape: str 1..512 (link title), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no link title
text: The title of the comment box link. Absent means no title.

name: CommentBoxAnchor
text: Where the leader line of a comment box points; kind selects a free point, a task or a highlight box.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[*].kind
text: freePoint: a place on the chart that is tied to nothing; task: one of eight points of a task figure; highlightBox: one of eight points of a highlight box.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[freePoint].dateTime
shape: DateTime "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS", required in freePoint; not held while snapped
text: The point in time where the tip stands on the time axis.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[freePoint].taskGroupId
text: The task group whose band holds the tip; in a fallback, the task group where the tip goes when its target is deleted.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[freePoint].bandFraction
text: The height of the tip within that task group's band: 0 is the top edge, 1 the bottom edge.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[task].taskUid
text: The uid of the task that the tip is snapped to.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[task].figure
text: Which figure of the task the tip is snapped to: the plan bar, the actual bar or the milestone.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[task].point
shape: enum 8 points, required in task and highlightBox
text: Which of the eight points of the target the tip is snapped to: the four corners and the middles of the four sides.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[task].fallback
text: Where the tip goes when the task is deleted.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[highlightBox].highlightBoxId
text: The id of the highlight box that the tip is snapped to.

name: CommentBoxAnchor/oneOf[highlightBox].fallback
text: Where the tip goes when the highlight box is deleted.

name: AnchorFallback
text: The task group and the height in its band where the tip goes when its target is deleted.

name: HighlightBox
text: One highlight box. Encloses a range of dates and task groups.

name: HighlightBox.id
text: The id of the highlight box.

name: HighlightBox.topTaskGroupId
text: The task group at the top edge of the box.

name: HighlightBox.bottomTaskGroupId
text: The task group at the bottom edge of the box.

name: HighlightBox.firstDay
text: The first day that the box covers (included), as a day of the schedule data clock.

name: HighlightBox.lastDay
text: The last day that the box covers (included).

name: HighlightBox.cornerRadiusPx
text: Corner radius of the highlight box, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100 (0 to 24; 0 is a square corner; GRS writes 4 when it places a box). It follows displayScalePercent; zoom does not change it.

name: HighlightBox.fillColor
text: Fill color of the highlight box; fillTransparencyPercent 100 draws no fill.

name: HighlightBox.fillTransparencyPercent
text: Transparency of the highlight box fill in percent: 0 is opaque, 100 draws no fill.

name: HighlightBox.strokeColor
shape: $ref Color, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no frame line
text: Frame color of the highlight box. Absent means no frame line is drawn (the frame can still be grabbed).

name: HighlightBox.strokeWidthPx
text: Border width of the highlight box, in CSS pixels at displayScalePercent 100 (1 to 10; GRS writes 1 when it places a box). It follows displayScalePercent; zoom does not change it.

name: DocumentStamp
text: When the document last changed and was saved, and who wrote it last. These instants live outside schedule and documentSettings so that writing them never moves either group's clock.

name: DocumentStamp.scheduleUpdatedAt
text: When the schedule data last changed. A watcher of changes looks only at this time.

name: DocumentStamp.documentUpdatedAt
text: When the document last changed, in the schedule data or in documentSettings.

name: DocumentStamp.fileSavedAt
shape: UtcInstant, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: never written to a file
text: When this document was last written to its file. Absent until it has been written once. It is in documentStamp, not in schedule.project, so that a save does not change scheduleUpdatedAt. It is UTC so that each reader sees it in their own local time. MS Project's LastSaved is not stored; GRS makes it at the moment of export. So the save time is held in one place, and a save never counts as a schedule change.

name: DocumentStamp.lastEditedBy
text: Who wrote the document last: {"kind":"user"} for a person on the screen, {"kind":"template"} for the shipped start-up template, {"kind":"agent","name":...} for an Agent API caller.

name: Writer
text: Who wrote: a person on the screen, the shipped start-up template, or an Agent API caller.

name: Writer/oneOf[*].kind
text: user: a person on the screen; template: the shipped start-up template; agent: an Agent API caller.

name: Writer/oneOf[agent].name
text: The name that the Agent API caller gave for itself.

name: ChangeLogEntry
text: Why a change was made; the conversation that led to it is not stored.

name: ChangeLogEntry.ordinal
text: The order of this entry in the document.

name: ChangeLogEntry.changedAt
text: When the change was made.

name: ChangeLogEntry.editedBy
text: Who made the change.

name: ChangeLogEntry.explanation
text: Why the change was made.

name: PassthroughValues
text: Values of an imported MS Project element that GRS does not interpret, kept under their own names and written back unchanged; only the MS Project export and its notices read them. GRS adds two keys of its own: xmlns (the namespace of the file) and #StopCountedFrom (the ActualDuration that stop was counted from).

name: PassthroughElement
text: One element of an imported MS Project file that GRS does not interpret, kept as it arrived so that it is written back unchanged.

name: PassthroughElement.ordinal
text: The order of this element within its owner, used to write it back in its place.

name: PassthroughElement.name
text: The element name in the MS Project file, spelled exactly as it came.

name: PassthroughElement.fields
shape: map str->str<=65535 (>=1 entry), optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no leaves
text: The leaf values of the element, by their names.

name: PassthroughElement.children
shape: PassthroughElement[], optional: omit the property when there are no items; never write [] (minItems 1)
text: The child elements nested in this element.

name: Day
text: A date without a time of day; each key that uses it says which clock the day is on.

name: DateTime
text: A wall-clock date-time in project.scheduleDataTimeZone, written without an offset, as MS Project writes it; an offset in an imported file is dropped.

name: Time
text: A time of day, as MS Project writes it.

name: UtcInstant
text: A point in time in UTC, to the second.

name: UtcOffset
text: A fixed offset from UTC, written as a standard-time key such as UTC+09:00; daylight saving is never applied by season.

name: Color
shape: oneOf theme|palette|custom (no none: an absent colour key is "not drawn")
text: A color: theme uses the color that the theme gives this place, palette names a palette color, custom gives its own values for the light and the dark theme. An absent color key means that nothing is drawn.

name: Color/oneOf[*].kind
text: theme: the color that the theme gives this place; palette: a named palette color; custom: its own values for the light and the dark theme.

name: Color/oneOf[palette].name
text: The palette color, by its stored name.

name: Color/oneOf[custom].light
shape: $ref ColorSide, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: GRS derives it on load
text: The color for the light theme; at least one of light and dark is present.

name: Color/oneOf[custom].dark
shape: $ref ColorSide, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: GRS derives it on load
text: The color for the dark theme; at least one of light and dark is present.

name: ColorSide
text: One side of a custom color: its value, and whether a person chose it or GRS derived it.

name: ColorSide.value
text: The color value for this theme.

name: ColorSide.source
text: chosen: a person chose this value; derived: GRS derived it from the other side when it loaded the document (HSL lightness 1 - L).

name: BandColor
text: The color of a task group band: the same as Color, except that the palette color ink is not offered.

name: ColumnFilter
text: A filter on one column of a table: values hides rows by their shown value, dateRange hides rows whose date is outside a range of days.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[*].kind
text: values: hide rows by their shown value; dateRange: hide rows whose date is outside firstDay..lastDay.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[*].column
text: The column that the filter is on, by its stable column name.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[values].hiddenValues
shape: str[] (shown text, or stable status/type names) 1.., optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no value hidden
text: The values whose rows are hidden; a status or a type is given by its stable name, any other value by its shown text.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[values].isBlankHidden
text: Whether the rows with an empty cell in this column are hidden.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[dateRange].firstDay
shape: Day, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no lower bound
text: The first day that is kept (included), as a day of the schedule data clock.

name: ColumnFilter/oneOf[dateRange].lastDay
shape: Day, optional (not in required); when the property is absent: no upper bound
text: The last day that is kept (included).

name: ColumnSort
text: How a table is sorted: by one column, in one direction.

name: ColumnSort.column
text: The column that the table is sorted by, by its stable column name.

name: ColumnSort.direction
text: The direction of the sort.

name: ColumnKey
shape: enum of stable column names of T-331/T-347/T-371
text: The stable English name of a table column; each table takes only the names of its own columns.

name: editProject
shape: {"kind":"editProject","set":{...},"clear":[...]} -- no id property (there is one per document)
text: Edits the project of the document. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `title`, `name`, `subject`, `category`, `company`, `manager`, `author`, `revision`, `startDate`, `statusDate`, `themeHue`, `parentTaskProgressToleranceWorkingDays` and `scheduleDataTimeZone`. `clear` takes all of them except `themeHue`, `parentTaskProgressToleranceWorkingDays` and `scheduleDataTimeZone`; without `statusDate`, no status date line is drawn. Setting `scheduleDataTimeZone` does not convert: the stored numbers stay the same and only the zone they are read in changes.

name: shiftScheduleTimes
text: Shifts all schedule date-times at once by `minutes` (positive moves later, negative moves earlier). It is one write; the columns it rewrites and the ones it leaves untouched are fixed by the specification.\nWhen it arrives from the Agent API, it is applied without asking the person for confirmation.

name: shiftScheduleToStartDate
shape: newStartDay ($defs/Day "YYYY-MM-DD") -- assumes that the value name and type follow Day in findings 09/12
text: Moves the whole schedule to start on the day `newStartDay` (YYYY-MM-DD), shifting by working days. It is one write; which columns move, what stays, and how the move is made are fixed by the specification.\nWhen it arrives from the Agent API, it is applied as sent without asking, the same as `shiftScheduleTimes`.

name: replaceCalendarRules
shape: the same 4 (when one is omitted, that part stays as it is)
text:
Edits the calendar: the working weekdays, one set of working times for a working day, the exception days, and the day the week starts on.
`workingDayTypes` lists the working weekdays (1 is Sunday; weekdays not listed are days off). `weekStartDay` is the day the week starts on. `exceptions` is the complete list of exception days after the edit. `workingTimes` is one set of working times for a working day.
If the document still has the default calendar, create a calendar first and then edit it.
The times of `fromDate` and `toDate` of an exception day are aligned by the side that writes the command into the document.
`workingTimes` holds 1 to 5 spans: an empty list is refused. To go back to the default working times, pass the two default spans 08:00:00-12:00:00 and 13:00:00-17:00:00.

name: editTask
shape: {"kind":"editTask","taskUid":7,"set":{...},"clear":[...]} -- the properties include set.hyperlinkAddress (URL, 1..512 characters) / set.hyperlink (title, 1..512 characters) / clear ["hyperlinkAddress","hyperlink"]
text: Edits the task `taskUid`. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `name`, `notes`, `start`, `finish`, `deadline`, `fadeInCalendarDays`, `fadeOutCalendarDays`, `parentTaskUid`, `hyperlinkAddress` and `hyperlink`; `clear` takes all of them except `start` and `finish`. The rules are checked on the task after the edit; when `start` or `finish` moves, `percentComplete` and `passthroughValues` are worked out again. `set.name` does not change the name of any task group. A `hyperlinkAddress` that starts with `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:`, read as a browser reads it, is refused (`hyperlinkSchemeNotAllowed`).

name: createTask
shape: exactly one of taskShape (rectangle|chevron|arrow|endpointSpan) or milestoneShape (diamond or another name in SH-5) (oneOf), start, finish (DateTime), taskGroupId
text:
Creates an unnamed task with the given `taskShape` or `milestoneShape`, `start` and `finish`, placed on the task group `taskGroupId`.
Give exactly one of `taskShape` (`rectangle`, `chevron`, `arrow` or `endpointSpan`) and `milestoneShape` (one of the 15 glyphs); `milestoneShape` makes the task a milestone.
The new task's uid is `project.highestIssuedUid` plus 1, and `highestIssuedUid` moves to it, so a later command of the same batch that creates something with a uid takes the next number.
Example: when `highestIssuedUid` is 41, the batch [`createTask`, `createTask`, `editTask` with `taskUid` 42 and `set.name`, `editTask` with `taskUid` 43 and `set.name`] names both new tasks.
A `taskGroupId` that names no task group makes a new top-level task group with that id.

name: pasteTasks
text: Duplicates the tasks listed in `sourceUids`. Descendant tasks that are not among the carried tasks are not copied.\n`landing` is sent only for a Ctrl-drag copy; it carries where the copy is placed.

name: moveTaskToTaskGroup
text: Moves the task `taskUid` to another task group `taskGroupId`.

name: placeTaskPlanActual
text: Sets the five plan-and-actual columns of the task `taskUid` as described by `place`.

name: beginTaskActual
text: Starts recording the actual of the task `taskUid` after a plan-and-actual grab handle was dragged.\n`grabbed` names the handle that was grabbed, `released` is where it was let go, and `snapMinutes` is the snap step in minutes that sets the length of the dummy actual.

name: cycleTaskPlanActualState
shape: taskUid, remembered? (RememberedActual; omit the property when no actual is remembered), snapMinutes?
text: Advances the plan-and-actual state of the task `taskUid` by one step along the state cycle.\nWhen going back from interrupted to not started, the actual that was removed is remembered by the screen state and passed in as `remembered`; omit `remembered` when no actual is remembered. `snapMinutes` is the snap step in minutes; when omitted, the day step is used.

name: deleteTask
text: Deletes the task `taskUid`.

name: createDependency
text: Draws a dependency line from the task `predecessorUid` to the task `successorUid`.\n`predecessorEdge` and `successorEdge` name the ends (start or finish); the pair of ends decides the link type.\nIf either task is a milestone, the line is always finish-to-start, whatever `predecessorEdge` and `successorEdge` say.

name: changeDependencyLag
shape: predecessorUid, successorUid, lag ({"kind":"workingDays","workingDays":n} | {"kind":"typed","minutes":n,"unit":"day|hour|minute"}) -- the union shape and its words are assumed
text: Changes the lag of the dependency from `predecessorUid` to `successorUid`. `lag` is one of {"kind":"workingDays","workingDays"} (a working-day lag) and {"kind":"typed","minutes","unit"} (a typed lag; `unit` is `day`, `hour` or `minute`).

name: deleteDependency
text: Deletes the dependency lines from `predecessorUid` to `successorUid`. Every line in that direction is deleted; to delete only one, use `deleteDependencyAt`.

name: deleteDependencyAt
text: Deletes one dependency line among those in the same direction, named by `successorUid`, `predecessorUid` and its position `order` (0 is the first) in the successor's list of dependencies.\nRefused if no such line exists. Lines in the same direction have no name of their own, so the position in the list is the only way to name one.

name: editResource
text: Edits the resource `resourceUid`. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). The only property is `name`: `set.name` renames the resource, and clearing `name` leaves it unnamed.

name: createResource
text: Adds a resource named `name`.

name: deleteResources
text: Deletes the resources listed in `resourceUids`.

name: deleteUnreferencedResources
text: Deletes all resources that no assignment refers to.

name: createAssignment
text: Assigns the resource `resourceUid` to the task `taskUid`.

name: deleteAssignment
text: Removes the assignment of the resource `resourceUid` from the task `taskUid`.

name: editTaskGroup
shape: {"kind":"editTaskGroup","taskGroupId":"...","set":{...},"clear":[...]} -- the properties include set.hyperlinkAddress (URL, 1..512 characters) / set.hyperlink (title, 1..512 characters) / clear ["hyperlinkAddress","hyperlink"]
text: Edits the task group `taskGroupId`. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `name`, `color`, `minHeightPx`, `treeState`, `editGroup`, `hyperlinkAddress` and `hyperlink`; `clear` takes all of them except `treeState`, and without `color` no band color is painted. `name` is plain text and does not follow the name of the represented task; a task group may have no name. `editGroup` is not implemented yet: setting or clearing it is refused (`notImplemented`). `hyperlinkAddress` follows the same rule as in `editTask`.

name: createTaskGroup
shape: id, parentId? (when omitted: top level), name? (string 1..512), representedTaskUid?, siblingOrder
text: Creates a task group with the given `id`, `siblingOrder` and, when given, `parentId` (absent: top level), `name` (absent: unnamed) and `representedTaskUid`.

name: pasteTaskGroupSubtree
shape: sourceTaskGroupId, parentId? (when omitted: top level), newTaskGroupIds (map)
text: Duplicates the subtree of task groups rooted at `sourceTaskGroupId`, placing the copy of the root under `parentId` (absent: top level).\n`newTaskGroupIds` maps each source `id` to the `id` of its copy.

name: reorderTaskGroupSiblings
text: Reorders the sibling task groups under `parentId` (absent means the top level) into the order given by `orderedIds`. That order becomes their `siblingOrder`.

name: moveTaskGroup
shape: taskGroupId, parentId? (when omitted: top level), siblingOrder
text: Changes the parent and the place among its siblings of the task group `taskGroupId` to `parentId` (absent: top level) and `siblingOrder`.

name: resetTaskGroupTreeStates
text: Returns the tree state of every task group to `auto`, except task groups that are hidden.

name: deleteTaskGroup
text: Deletes the task group `taskGroupId`.\nWhen it deletes the last task group, a new top-level task group named `Untitled` is made, because the document always has at least one task group.

name: editTaskVisual
shape: {"kind":"editTaskVisual","taskUid":7,"set":{...},"clear":[...]} -- clear takes only the 2 colour properties
text: Edits how the task `taskUid` is drawn. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `taskShape`, `milestoneShape`, `fillColor`, `strokeColor` and `strokeWidthPx`; `clear` takes only `fillColor` and `strokeColor`, and a color that is absent is not drawn. `taskShape` is only for a task that is not a milestone, and `milestoneShape` is only for a milestone; the wrong one is refused (`milestoneShapeMismatch`). A task left with neither `fillColor` nor `strokeColor` is refused (`fillAndStrokeBothInvisible`). To follow the theme again, set the color to {"kind":"theme"}.

name: editCommentBox
shape: {"kind":"editCommentBox","commentBoxId":"...","set":{...},"clear":["text","hyperlinkAddress","hyperlink"]} -- the properties include set.hyperlinkAddress (URL, 1..512 characters) / set.hyperlink (title, 1..512 characters) / clear ["hyperlinkAddress","hyperlink"]
text: Edits the comment box `commentBoxId`. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `text`, `anchor`, `bodyOffsetPx`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidthPx`, `fillColor`, `fillTransparencyPercent`, `textColor`, `fontSizePx`, `hyperlinkAddress` and `hyperlink`; `clear` takes only `text`, `hyperlinkAddress` and `hyperlink`. `anchor` has the same shape as in `createCommentBox`. The frame, the text and the fill always have a color; to hide the fill, set `fillTransparencyPercent` to 100. `hyperlinkAddress` follows the same rule as in `editTask`.

name: createCommentBox
shape: commentBoxId, anchor ({"kind":"freePoint","dateTime","taskGroupId","bandFraction"} | {"kind":"task","taskUid","figure","point","fallback":{"taskGroupId","bandFraction"}} | {"kind":"highlightBox","highlightBoxId","point","fallback":{...}} -- every property inside is required)
text: Places a comment box with the given `commentBoxId`, attached as `anchor` says.\n`anchor` is one of {"kind":"freePoint","dateTime","taskGroupId","bandFraction"}, {"kind":"task","taskUid","figure","point","fallback"} and {"kind":"highlightBox","highlightBoxId","point","fallback"}; every key of the chosen kind is required.

name: bringCommentBoxToFront
text: Moves the comment box `commentBoxId` to the end of the list of comment boxes, which is the front-most position.

name: deleteCommentBox
text: Deletes the comment box `commentBoxId`.

name: editHighlightBox
text: Edits the highlight box `highlightBoxId`. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `firstDay`, `lastDay`, `topTaskGroupId`, `bottomTaskGroupId`, `strokeColor`, `strokeWidthPx`, `fillColor` and `fillTransparencyPercent`; `clear` takes only `strokeColor`, and without it no frame line is drawn. The rules are checked on the box after the edit. A box whose last day or bottom task group comes before its first day or top task group is refused (`highlightBoxInverted`). A box with no `strokeColor` and `fillTransparencyPercent` 100 is refused (`fillAndStrokeBothInvisible`).

name: createHighlightBox
shape: highlightBoxId, firstDay, lastDay ($defs/Day), topTaskGroupId, bottomTaskGroupId -- the range wrapper is removed, and the property names follow the property names in the document (finding 09)
text: Places a highlight box with the given `highlightBoxId`, enclosing the days from `firstDay` to `lastDay` (both included) and the task groups from `topTaskGroupId` to `bottomTaskGroupId`.

name: bringHighlightBoxToFront
text: Moves the highlight box `highlightBoxId` to the end of the list of highlight boxes, which is the front-most position.

name: deleteHighlightBox
text: Deletes the highlight box `highlightBoxId`.

name: editDocumentSettings
shape: {"kind":"editDocumentSettings","set":{...},"clear":[...]} -- no id property. clear takes fitSpan and displayTimeZones
text: Edits the document settings, which say how the schedule is shown. `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes every property of `documentSettings` except `pinnedTaskGroupIds` (use `pinTaskGroup` and `unpinTaskGroup`) and `tableViews` (use `editTableView`); `clear` takes only `fitSpan` and `displayTimeZones`. `fitSpan` is written whole, with `firstDay`, `lastDay` and `isFixed`; clearing it also removes the fixing. Setting `viewTimeZone` converts only the shown times; the stored values stay the same.

name: pinTaskGroup
text: Pins the task group `taskGroupId` by adding it to the pinned task groups.

name: unpinTaskGroup
text: Unpins the task group `taskGroupId` by removing it from the pinned task groups. When the last one is removed, the `pinnedTaskGroupIds` property is removed too; [] is never written.

name: fitScheduleToScreenOnPage
text:
Fits the whole schedule to the screen of the page, as the Fit button does: the page computes the zoom and the scroll position from its own screen size, so you need not know it.
The page computes them from the screen as drawn before this batch, so send it in a batch of its own after the edits that change the rows.
It does not unfold the task groups as the Fit button also does; to unfold them, send resetTaskGroupTreeStates in an earlier batch.
It is refused while the page has not drawn its screen yet.

name: editTableView
text: Edits how one table looks; `table` names it (`searchPanel`, `delayDiagnosticsReport` or `resourceList`). `set` writes the listed properties and `clear` removes the listed optional ones; a property in both is refused (`fieldSetAndCleared`). `set` takes `isScheduleFilterApplied`, `shownTaskUids`, `shownResourceUids`, `isUnassignedShown`, `columnFilters` and `sort`, but only the ones the named table has; `clear` takes `shownTaskUids`, `shownResourceUids`, `columnFilters` and `sort`. Clearing a list means it has no items, and clearing `sort` returns the table to its default order. A property that the named table does not have is refused (`malformedRequest`).

name: member (the tool or member name, for example "applyCommands") and from ("page" | "relay")
text: member: which call was refused. from: who refused it.

name: message (both)
text: A human-readable explanation in English. It contains no row ids.

name: stamp -- present only when from is "page"
text: The current stamp (the document is not included, AG-2).

name: commandRefusals (only when reason is commandRefused) / documentFaults (only for schemaViolation and documentInvalid)
text: commandRefusals: one refusal for each refused command. documentFaults: one refusal for each fault in the imported document.

name: commandIndex (the position in the batch, from 0) and kind (the command name)
text: Which command was refused.

name: reason (a name from the command rows below)
text: Why the command was refused.

name: documentFaults[].at (JSON Pointer)
text: The place in the document that has the fault.

name: field (which value in the command, for example "set.start")
text: The value that was refused.

name: staleStamp
text: The stamp you passed differs from the current stamp in at least one value.

name: notOwnStep
text: The step to undo or redo was written by a different writer, not by the caller.

name: gestureInFlight
text: A person is in the middle of a drag that changes the document.

name: editingInPlace
text: A person is typing in place and has not confirmed the input yet.

name: questionAsked
text: The page is asking the person a confirmation question.

name: deliveringNotices
text: The page is in the middle of delivering change notices.

name: commandRefused
text: A command in the batch was refused, so no command in the batch was applied.

name: unknownTask
text: No task has the uid you named.

name: notDrawnYet
text: The page has not drawn the screen even once yet.

name: tooTall
text: The picture is taller than the height that can be exported.

name: rasterFailed
text: The page could not turn the picture into an image.

name: embeddedHtmlFailed
text: The page could not build the single .html file.

name: notAvailable
text: This page does not have the part that answers this member.

name: malformedRequest
text: The shape of the call or of a command does not match the schema.

name: historyEmpty
text: The history has no step to undo (or to redo).

name: nothingToIssue
text: There is no fix proposal to apply.

name: importNotLanded
text: The import did not land: the person canceled it, an open was in progress, or it did not pass validation (MM-4, OP-5, OP-8).

name: schemaViolation
text: The GRS JSON you passed does not match the schema (a uid outside 0..2147483647 also counts, JDG-3284).

name: formatTooNew
text: schemaVersion is newer than the newest version this build knows, and the document does not match the schema.

name: formatTooOld
text: schemaVersion is older than the version this build reads (an alpha document). This build has no conversion for old versions.

name: documentInvalid
text: The import validation (FR-023 and its limits) refused the document.

name: retiredName
text: A retired name was sent (a command kind, a member name, an argument name or an edit field name).

name: pageNotConnected
text: No GRS page is connected to the relay.

name: relayTimedOut
text: The page did not answer before the time limit.

name: badFileName
text: fileName is not a relative file name inside the save folder.

name: fileExists
text: The file already exists, and overwrite true was not given.

name: saveFolderUnavailable
text: The save folder cannot be made, read or written.

name: malformedRequest
text: The shape of which, defs or full for readSchema is wrong.

name: (retiredName)
text: An unknown tool name.

name: duplicateKey
text: A primary key value appears twice in the same array.

name: danglingReference
text: A foreign key points to a row that is not in the document.

name: pinnedTaskGroupMissing
text: A pinned task group does not exist.

name: taskParentCycle
text: The task parent links form a cycle.

name: taskGroupTooDeep
text: Task groups are nested deeper than the depth limit.

name: taskGroupMembershipBroken
text: A task is not in exactly one task group.

name: noCalendar
text: There is no calendar.

name: (retired)
text: TaskGroup name and derivedFromTaskUid are both null. JDG-3315 (a name is not required) retires this whole row. A task group with no name and no task it stands for is allowed.

name: fillAndStrokeBothInvisible
text: The fill and the stroke are both invisible. For TaskVisual, the fillColor and strokeColor properties are both absent. For HighlightBox, the strokeColor property is absent and the transparency is 100 (rewritten by JDG-3310).

name: endBeforeStart
text: A task's finish is before its start.

name: fadeWithoutFinish
text: A task that has a fade has no finish.

name: fadeLongerThanTask

name: unusableDate
text: A day or time column cannot be read, or is outside the accepted days.

name: importSequenceAhead
text: TaskOrigin.lastSeenImportSequence is greater than Project.importSequence.

name: settingOutOfBounds
text: A setting value does not meet a lower or upper limit that names another setting value.

name: calendarWithoutWorkingDay
text: The document calendar has no working weekday.

name: taskGroupParentCycle
text: The task group parent links form a cycle.

name: highlightBoxInverted
text: In a highlight box, firstDay is after lastDay, or the top task group is below the bottom task group.

name: noTaskGroup
text: There is no task group.

name: negativeActualLength
text: An actual length is below 0 (the actual work ends before it starts).

name: milestoneShapeMismatch
text: The shape properties do not match Task.milestone: a milestone has taskShape or has no milestoneShape, or the reverse (JDG-3311 rewrites the current IV-22).

name: taskVisualCountNotOne

name: invalidWorkingTimes
text: The number, the order or the overlap of the time ranges in a day breaks the rules.

name: fileTooLarge

text: The number of tasks to import is more than the limit (S-114).

name: taskWithoutDates

text: The named row (a task, task group, box, resource, assignment or dependency) does not exist.

text: The id of the row to make is already in use.

text: The dependency or assignment you tried to make already exists.

name: unusableDate
text: A day or time cannot be read, or is outside the accepted days.

text: A number is out of range, or is not an integer or not a finite number.

name: hyperlinkSchemeNotAllowed
text: The link address (hyperlinkAddress) starts with javascript:, vbscript: or data:. The check runs after the same normalization a browser does (JDG-3185: remove spaces and control characters at both ends, and make the scheme lower case) (JDG-3314).

text: You tried to move an item under its own subtree.
